title: IAM principals: user, group, service account and workload identity

videos.script: IAM never grants anything to a password, or to a laptop. It grants a role to a principal. {{principal}} A principal is written with a prefix, and the prefix says what kind of thing you are trusting. {{prefix}} User is one person, signed in. Group is everybody in a group, right now. {{people}} Grant to groups. The day somebody leaves, one change in the directory ends every role they had. {{groups}} Then there are two words that sound careful and are not. All authenticated users means every Google account in the world. {{everybody}} Programs get service accounts. Some you create, one for each workload. Some Google creates for itself, and those you leave alone. {{machines}} And some identities come from outside, from another company's directory or a CI system. Their names are long, because they have to say exactly who. {{outside}} In your lab, the provider refuses an address with no prefix. Then it plans one grant for each kind of principal. {{end}}
